title: Singur dam, a Hyderabad water source, drops below 2 TMC ft

slides.head: Singur dam, a Hyderabad water source, drops below 2 TMC ft
What happened
slides.body: Storage stood at 1.95 TMC ft on Monday against a full capacity of 29.91 TMC ft, after the project received only 3.56 TMC ft this year.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: Poor rain in the Manjeera catchment, and storage capped at 16 TMC ft last year on dam safety panel advice for repairs.

slides.head: Singur storage on Monday
slides.body: Last year it got its heaviest inflow in 29 years, 237 TMC ft; this year just 3.56.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: Singur also touched dead storage in 2018-19 and 2019-20.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: HMWSSB stops drawing at 0.8 TMC ft; officials expected about 1 TMC ft by end-December. Ask: Which other reservoirs will Hyderabad lean on if Singur stops?

slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

Singur dam, a Hyderabad water source, drops below 2 TMC ft

Singur reservoir, which supplies drinking water to Hyderabad, erstwhile Medak and Nizamabad, has fallen below 2 TMC ft for the first time in six years.

Why it matters: Poor rain in the Manjeera catchment, and storage capped at 16 TMC ft last year on dam safety panel advice for repairs.

Source: Telangana Today. Image: Telangana Today
